So the phrase 2 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 23.8. let her be polluted with blood, and without respect to her former holiness let us enter, sack and destroy her Temple and Palaces.</ns0:note>, and let our eye look upon <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">With delighting our selves in the ruine, let us feed our envious revengeful eye.</ns0:note> Zion <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">Upon <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> the Royal Palace, and the sacred Temple buried in their own rubbish.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 But they <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">The gathered confederate Nations, <ns0:hi>Zions</ns0:hi> Enemies.</ns0:note> know not <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther discern nor consider.</ns0:note> the thoughts of the LORD <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The design of the holy, just, gracious and faithful God who is God of his people, of <ns0:hi>Israel,</ns0:hi> who will humble but not extirpate, who will purifie by, but not consume in, the Furnace; Gods thoughts to <ns0:hi>Israel</ns0:hi> is to give him an expected end.</ns0:note>, neither understand they his counsel <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The same thing in somewhat diffe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rent phrase, this elegancy ever is added to confirm the thing foretold.</ns0:note>: for he shall gather them <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">By his secret, just, and effectual providence dispo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sing all things to facilitate their gathering together, that they shall do, and yet God also shall do it, he as the first cause, they as the second, he moves according to his own pleasure, they move as they are second and dependent Agents, they shall as a fire purge out the drosse, or a wind blow away the chaff and lightest Corn, which is that God intendeth, but they consult onely to extinguish the people, to cut them off that they be no more a Nation.</ns0:note> as the sheaves into the floor <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">A plain and very intelligible simile. The Husbandman gathers the sheaves into the floor to thresh them; so God gathers. <ns0:hi>i. e.</ns0:hi> in due time he will do this and bring his Enemies, and his Churches Enemies together that they may be bruised, broken and destroyed utterly. This seems to look to <ns0:hi>Sennacheribs</ns0:hi> gathering his power against <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> and the cir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumstances <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ell enough suit this, yet is not this to be confined or restrained to <ns0:hi>Sennacherib,</ns0:hi> but perhaps to the slaughter made on the Enemies in one hundred twenty seven Provinces in <ns0:hi>Esthers</ns0:hi> time, looking to somewhat that is farther off, indeed running through all ages of the Church, and shall be finally accomplisht in the ruin of the Antichristian Kingdom, then shall that of <ns0:hi>Zech.</ns0:hi> 12.3. be fulfilled, when though all Nations gather them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves against <ns0:hi>Ierusalem,</ns0:hi> yet 'tis that they may be cut in pieces, when the Vine of the Earth shall be gathered into the Wine<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />press of Gods wrath, <ns0:hi>Revel.</ns0:hi> 14.19, 20. and <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 19.15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 Arise <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">This imperative may be read in the future tense, and so be an express promise, it is however an implicite promise made to the Daughter of <ns0:hi>Zion,</ns0:hi> the Jewish Church, Type of the Gospel Catholick Church, that she shall be raised out of a captive, low and oppressed state, and this shall be by the reviving power of her God.</ns0:note> and thresh <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">So in a decorum to the Metaphor <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 12. used to express the gathering of the Enemy into the floor to be broken<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> the future strength of the Church employed successfully, (more by the arm of her Redeemer then her own) in the subduing and breaking her Enemies is here foretold and promised, as 'tis also <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 41.15. Christ will thus punish his Enemies, so <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> Ty<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pical as threatned <ns0:hi>Ier.</ns0:hi> 51.33. was beat to pieces, and so shall Antitypical <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> in due time be broken as straw that is thresht into smallest pieces like chaff.</ns0:note>, O daughter of Zi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on: for I will make thine horn Iron <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Some taking this for the horny part of the hoof of the Oxe which did tread out the Corn, make it to be in sense the same with the hoofs made brass, but they that take it as our Version doth for the horn properly taken, with which the horned beasts do push and thrust down, break or wound, do express the power and strength of the Church firm as Iron to beat down her Enemies.</ns0:note>, and I will make thy hoofs brass <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">By this figurative speech is the strength of <ns0:hi>Zion</ns0:hi> expressed, by which she treads under foot, and breaks the power of Enemies into pieces that it shall never be repaired, as straw that is thresht in the floor and broken like chaffe.</ns0:note>, and thou shalt beat in pieces <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">In the times after the re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />building of <ns0:hi>Ierusalem</ns0:hi> the Jews grew to such strength that in their Wars they did especially in the <ns0:hi>Maccabees</ns0:hi> times break their Enemies in pieces. But here is a mystical and spiritual sense of these words, as they refer to the <ns0:hi>Messiah</ns0:hi>'s Kingdom in which he will break hard hearts by the power of his word, and con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vert sinners to himself. And by the power of his Almighty arm will defend and support his own subjects, whilst he doth by in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vincible strength throw down and trample into dust his and their Enemies, and this power he hath sometimes evidently exercised already in the various deliverances he hath wrought for his people which stand recorded in the Church Histories, of this strength you may truly say what is reported of the inscrip<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion in the cross appearing to <ns0:hi>Constantine. In this thou shalt con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />quer.</ns0:hi>
